phantom mode transmission method can be applied for G.fast transmission system, however, the performance improvement is limited.

the phantom mode transmission method is not beneficial in the FEXT dominating scenario for the cable binder under consideration and that the phantom mode method is beneficial in the case of eliminated FEXT contributions.
the G.fast performance in a multi-quad cable binder is significantly better in case of phantom mode transmissions than in the standard mode of operation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the estimation of G.fast transmission performances over phantom modes in various scenarios.
the estimation of the G.fast transmission performance for phantom mode transmission over a metallic cable.
the estimation of the G.fast performance over phantom modes for various real scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phantom mode transmissions can be applied in the case of G.fast, but only for a limited number of subscribers in a cable binder.
phantom mode transmission is not a good option for G.fast systems.
the phantom mode transmission method has a potential to improve the transmission performance of G.fast in the FEXT dominated scenario, especially for a large cable binder.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phantom mode transmission method can be a good alternative to the traditional G.fast transmission system for the scenarios with a high level of crosstalk, which is typical for the multi-quad cables.

the phantom mode transmission can provide significant improvements of transmission performance for G.fast over phantom scenarios, but only if the crosstalk is not eliminated by the cable binder design.
phantom mode transmission is not a good option in a metallic cable with a large number of subscribers, especially in the case of a high frequency G.fast system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phantom mode transmission method can be very beneficial in terms of FEXT reduction for G.fast systems, especially for large metallic cable binders with a high number of subscribers.
the G.fast transmission system with VDMT is not able to fully exploit the potential benefits of phantom modes, which are mostly limited by the FEXT.
G.fast over phantom mode is not suitable for the majority of the cases, but there is a small group of cases where G.fast over phantom can outperform G.fast over metallic cable.
